scope: Third optimization round: close the three concrete findings in the additional fingerprint audit

changes: Replace the 400 ms post-resume injection with a beforeScriptExecution debugger gate; queue enable, breakpoint and startup-resume commands in protocol order to avoid the Chrome 157 startup deadlock
Verify current UA, platform, core count, timezone and exposed network state at the real script breakpoint before resuming application code; disable Debugger afterward

Browser auto-attach owns Service Workers; page and iframe filters exclude them. Defensive extra sessions release their startup latch only after owner arming and detach through their real parent after verification

Parse only recognized historical prefix expressions, collect cached identities across parsed static module dependencies and retire their exact private token/revision checks, preserving registrations and application data
Reject unverified already-running workers, malformed recognized prefixes, incompatible same-token revisions, failed probes and timeouts. Source/graph limits remain bounded
Keep deferred network setup on its owning FingerprintSession rather than a global per-item session set
Correct the v2 10.1 Mbps pool slot to 10 Mbps without redrawing the seed or unrelated axes
Share native range/bucket projection between sanitization, document/worker injection and delivery verification: 0-10 Mbps by 0.05 Mbps; 0-3000 ms by 50 ms
Retain v1 serialized draws and report a legacy warning while delivering the corrected effective native reading; v2 inconsistent runtime configurations fail validation
Distinguish absent/null/blank/boolean inputs from numeric zero; preserve native API absence
Use a single custom-battery normalizer during save/load and generation; level zero remains zero
Preserve null as the JSON representation of unknown/Infinity and avoid inventing finite durations when custom values are absent
Enforce charging/discharging time semantics and zero chargingTime for a fully charged charging battery
Render unknown durations as blank in the editor and preserve them on save

finalAffectedReruns.reason: Add explicit no-refetch cache assertions, retain deferred network state on the owning session, and distinguish application function names from historical prefixes

validation.note: SW update tests close message ports and wait for native activation state changes rather than repeatedly messaging the old active worker during activation. An isolated raw/attach-only/gated module-worker update probe also activated successfully.

retainedFailureEvidence.symptom: CDP persistent socket error after the first native browser case
retainedFailureEvidence.cause: Unconfirmed; that run preceded detailed native browser exit telemetry
retainedFailureEvidence.followUp: Added browser exit/signal, engine-event and stderr diagnostics; three consecutive standalone reruns passed, followed by the final full-suite rerun reported above. No automatic retry was added to hide native failures.

behaviorChanges: Affected existing v2 downlink readings change from 10.1 to 10. V1 seeded default replay retains its historical serialized draw (240 fixtures unchanged); invalid live values and custom overrides are normalized to native bounds
Custom contradictory or unknown battery durations are normalized to valid native state semantics; invalid historical custom values do not retain their former live readings
Service Worker delivery can reject startup/targets when a pre-script identity cannot be verified; it never automatically deletes user registration or cache data
remainingLimits: Native Windows/macOS kernels, GPU/font behavior and arbitrary module graphs are not certified by Linux Chrome tests
Firefox blob/data, cached/local-bypass Worker first-instruction delivery and native Gecko TLS/HTTP2 transport remain outside this Chromium gate
Native bounds and deterministic coherence do not constitute an empirically calibrated real-device or network-quality distribution
No claim of perfect or universally indistinguishable fingerprint emulation
